basis: Brittle photosensitive hair/skin; intellectual disability 3/3, cataracts 2/3, hearing loss 1/3. GI/immune findings have single-case evidence and lose priority under the cap.
Congenital facial nerve palsy, sensorineural hearing loss and characteristic strabismus define the syndrome.
Bacterial infection; no particular organ site or common organ damage is established for this concept.
IgG4-mediated fibrosis; ureteral encasement with hydronephrosis/renal insufficiency and large-vessel vasculitis each occur in 30-79%. Skin infiltrates alone do not establish injury.
Latent treponemal infection; active cutaneous or skeletal injury is not intrinsic to the latent stage.
Inherited retinal degeneration; no syndromic extraocular involvement is specified.
Mitochondrial ATP synthesis disorder; encephalopathy, seizures and cerebellar hypoplasia in 2/2; pulmonary hypoplasia in 2/2. Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Chromosomal duplication syndrome with developmental impairment; variable cardiac, renal and skeletal malformations lack sufficient frequency evidence across this umbrella.
Hereditary spastic neurodegeneration classified as lysosomal storage disease. Bladder dysfunction is neurogenic; weakness and elevated CK do not establish primary muscle injury.
Lipid metabolism disorder; atherosclerosis and its organ complications are separately diagnosed diseases.
Porphyrin metabolism disorders; skin and neurologic injury depend on subtype and clinical penetrance. Neither is established as common across the entire umbrella.
Dysferlinopathies are skeletal muscle diseases, including limb-girdle and distal muscular dystrophies; the neurological ancestry does not establish nerve injury.
Smooth muscle malignancy arising in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis; histology does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Facial dermal melanocytic nevus; scleral pigmentation in about two-thirds does not itself impair function. Glaucoma and uveal melanoma are separate disease risks.
Genus-level bacterial infection umbrella; anatomical sites vary, without an established common site of direct damage across the group.
Mesenchymal tumor arising in and replacing renal parenchyma; spindle-cell histology does not establish muscle involvement.
Epithelial malignancy of the ovary, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no endocrine function or qualifying extraovarian damage is specified.
Congenital structural and functional underdevelopment of the stomach; associated malformations are unspecified and cannot support additional axes.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; cerebral/cerebellar atrophy, seizures and developmental impairment in 1/1; hepatic failure in 1/1. Evidence is limited to one annotated patient.
Severe insulin resistance defines an endocrine/metabolic disorder; acromegaloid appearance alone does not establish skeletal damage.
T-cell immunodeficiency with neutropenia in 2/2 supports blood involvement. Hepatomegaly alone is not liver injury; infections and associated autoimmune skin diseases are separately diagnosed.
Developmental impairment and movement abnormalities define the syndrome; esotropia occurs in 30-79%. Minor facial and external-ear differences do not establish functional organ injury.
Glandular epithelial malignancy arising in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no qualifying extraorgan involvement is specified.
Skeletal thoracic dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia is a major asphyxiating feature. Renal, pancreatic and cardiac involvement lacks established frequency for this subtype.
Inherited coagulation inhibitor deficiency; DVT and pulmonary embolism are separately diagnosed thrombotic complications. Osteonecrosis ancestry does not establish skeletal disease.
